speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: asked the Minister for Education whether the Government plans to (i) look into the survey findings of the Academic Freedom Survey 2021 published by AcademiaSG, notably that faculty who said they work on "politically sensitive" topics are more likely to feel constrained in their ability to research or engage the public, compared to those whose work are not "politically sensitive" and (ii) take steps to improve the state of academic freedom, especially in respect of Singapore studies and women academics, whom the survey reported as being more likely to feel constrained.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman) (for the Minister for Education)
text: Doing so has allowed them to attract top talent as well as to create new knowledge, innovate and contribute to Singapore's development over the past decades.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman) (for the Minister for Education)
text: The quality of education and research done by AUs is also well-regarded internationally.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman) (for the Minister for Education)
text: It would be unfair to our academics to assume that they self-censor or feel inhibited.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman) (for the Minister for Education)
text: The AUs' work on Singapore studies is evidence that academics do not shy away from "politically sensitive" topics.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman) (for the Minister for Education)
text: This includes titles, such as "Is the People's Action Party Here to Stay?" by Singh, 2019, and "Super-diversity and the Bio-politics of Migrant Worker Exclusion in Singapore" by Goh, 2019.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman) (for the Minister for Education)
text: Such works contribute to public discourse on governance and public policy and also inform the teaching curriculum.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman) (for the Minister for Education)
text: Many researchers in AUs also work with Government agencies to study complex issues.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman) (for the Minister for Education)
text: These projects, in turn, can be used or adapted as teaching materials for the students.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman) (for the Minister for Education)
text: So, it would be unfair to our academics, including female academics, to assume that they self-censor or feel inhibited.

speaker: Mr Speaker
